transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started. As we all know, the DOJ has issued a subpoena concerning commission payments made through our international distributors, and we need to provide an initial response and proposed investigation plan next month. I've reviewed the draft response, which describes the matter as involving international distributor commissions and proposes preserving relevant records and interviewing implicated personnel. Before I sign off on the submission, our standard legal-review process requires each of us at this roundtable to make any material factual confirmation relevant to the proposed response terms part of the formal meeting record. So I'd like to go around the table — please share anything material that bears on the accuracy or completeness of what we're proposing to tell DOJ. I'll start by noting that I have no private facts to disclose at this time. Who else is here, and what can each of you add?

transcript.text:
Thank you all for getting those material confirmations on the record. Let me summarize where we stand based on what's been disclosed today:

First, from Thomas: the subpoena scope is precisely four distributors covering calendar years 2019 through 2021, and our response packet has not yet been updated to reflect this. That needs to be corrected before submission.

Second, from Maya: finance has confirmed $275,000 in improper payments, with controllership sign-off obtained yesterday. Under our DOJ-response policy, once finance has confirmed improper payments and a repayment figure, we are required to authorize a voluntary disclosure in the initial response. That trigger has now been met.

Third, from Jordan: the implicated vice president has retained separate counsel and will not participate in a company interview without written consent from that counsel. Our draft response proposes interviewing implicated personnel, so we cannot represent an unrestricted interview plan without accounting for this constraint.

Given all three confirmations are now part of the formal meeting record, I believe we are in a position to settle the key decisions. Specifically: (1) we should authorize the voluntary disclosure in the initial response, given Maya's confirmed repayment figure; (2) the repayment amount is $275,000; (3) the investigation scope should be updated to reflect exactly four distributors, calendar years 2019 through 2021; and (4) the executive interview protocol must reflect the separate-counsel constraint. Before I proceed, does anyone have any additional material facts to add to the record, or any objection to settling on these terms?
